readings.heading: Ὁ Ἀπόστολος — 2 Corinthians 4:13–18
verses: 13. Brothers and sisters: we have the same spirit of faith as the scripture describes — "I believed, and so I spoke" — and we too believe, and so we also speak.
14. We know that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us too through Jesus, and will place us beside him together with you.
15. All these things are for your sake, so that grace, spreading to more and more people, may make thanksgiving overflow to the glory of God.
16. That is why we do not lose heart. Even if our outward self is wearing away, our inner self is being made new day by day.
17. This slight trouble of the moment is working out for us an eternal weight of glory that outweighs it beyond all measure —
18. because we keep our eyes not on what can be seen, but on what cannot be seen. What can be seen lasts only for a while; what cannot be seen lasts for ever.

readings.heading: Τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον — Matthew 24:27–33, 42–51
verses: 27. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: "Just as lightning comes out of the east and shines as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
28. Wherever the carcass is, there the vultures will gather.

29. And immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

30. And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven; and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with great power and glory.
31. And he will send out his angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
32. Now learn the lesson from the fig tree. When its branch has already become tender and it puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
33. In the same way, when you see all these things, you know that he is near, at the very doors.
42. So keep watch, because you do not know at what hour your Lord is coming.
43. But be sure of this: if the master of the house had known at what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have let his house be broken into.
44. That is why you too must be ready — the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
45. Who, then, is the faithful and sensible servant, the one his master has put in charge of his household, to give them their food at the proper time?
46. Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, will find doing just that.
47. Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of everything he owns.
48. But if that wicked servant says in his heart, 'My master is taking a long time to come,'
49. and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eats and drinks with the drunkards,
50. that servant's master will come on a day he does not expect, and at an hour he does not know,
51. and he will cut him in two, and assign him his share with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there."
